questions.q: The board has no barometer, and `baro_hardware` is left at `AUTO`. What does `status` show in INAV 9.1.0?
options: Nothing special: `AUTO` without a sensor quietly turns into `NONE`
The `HWFAIL` flag: the sensor is selected but not found, arming is disabled
The `NAV` flag: without a barometer navigation is considered unsafe
The `CAL` flag: the firmware waits for the barometer calibration forever
questions.explain: `getHwBarometerStatus()` returns “unavailable” if the requested sensor is not found, `isHardwareHealthy()` gives false, and `ARMING_DISABLED_HARDWARE_FAILURE` (`HWFAIL`) is set. The same rule applies to the rangefinder, the pitot and the flow. For a missing sensor set `NONE`.

questions.q: `rangefinder_hardware = VL53L1X` (a 27° cone). Roll 10°, pitch 10°, the driver returned 150 cm, `inav_max_surface_altitude = 200`. What does the estimator get?
options: 148 cm: 150 × cos 10°, the tilt on each axis is less than 13.5°
145 cm: 150 × cos 10° × cos 10°, the fractional part dropped
150 cm: at a tilt of less than 13.5° no compensation is applied
−1: the total tilt of 14.1° is greater than half the cone, 13.5°
questions.explain: cos θ = cos 10° × cos 10° = 0.9699, which is less than the threshold cos 13.5° = 0.9724. `rangefinderProcess()` replaces the reading with “out of range”, and the reliability gets a zero. The total tilt is compared, not the angles separately.

questions.q: The rangefinder is healthy and measuring, and there is no barometer on the board (`baro_hardware = NONE`). What about the AGL altitude?
options: The AGL quality is always LOW: the calculation requires a healthy barometer
AGL is computed as usual, the barometer does not affect it
AGL is computed, but with reduced `inav_w_z_surface_*` weights
AGL is taken straight from the rangefinder without filtering
questions.explain: In `estimationCalculateAGL()` the condition is `EST_SURFACE_VALID` and `EST_BARO_VALID` at the same time. Without a barometer the branch is executed in which AGL equals the general altitude and the quality is LOW. The SURFACE mode will not be in the list either: it requires both sensors.

questions.q: A multirotor in ALTHOLD with SURFACE on flew above `inav_max_surface_altitude`. The throttle is in the middle. What does INAV do?
options: It holds the current altitude on the barometer, like an ordinary ALTHOLD
It turns SURFACE off and returns altitude control to the pilot
It starts descending at 50 cm/s until AGL comes back
It climbs to `nav_max_terrain_follow_alt` and holds that altitude on the barometer
questions.explain: Readings above the limit are not accepted, the reliability falls, and AGL stops being trusted. `adjustMulticopterAltitudeFromRCInput()` sets a descent for this case: 50 cm/s with the throttle at the middle or above, up to 200 cm/s at idle. In the OSD — “(!SURFACE UNRELIABLE!)”.

questions.q: The aircraft has GPS with a good fix, optical flow and a rangefinder. How does the flow take part in the position estimate?
options: It is blended with GPS by the weights `inav_w_xy_flow_p` and `inav_w_xy_gps_p`
It replaces GPS at an altitude below `inav_max_surface_altitude`
It corrects only the velocity and leaves the position to GPS
It does not: while horizontal GPS is trusted, the flow is not called
questions.explain: In `updateEstimatedTopic()` the corrections are written as “GPS or flow”: `estimationCalculateCorrection_XY_GPS(&ctx) || estimationCalculateCorrection_XY_FLOW(&ctx)`. If GPS is trusted, the first function returns true and the second is not executed.

questions.q: How does INAV 9.1.0 obtain `opflow_scale` in the calibration from the Calibration tab?
options: The aircraft is carried over a known distance, and the flow is divided by the path
The aircraft is rocked in place for 30 s: the sum of the flow is divided by the sum of the gyro rate
The aircraft hovers still for 30 s, and the scale is fitted to the drift
The scale is read from the sensor over MSP with the first packet
questions.explain: For 30 seconds `opflowUpdate()` sums, over the valid samples, the magnitude of the flow in sensor units normalized to a second and the magnitude of the body rate in °/s; the scale is their ratio. It is saved if the sum of the body rates is greater than 3600. With rotation in place the flow has to equal the rotation.

questions.q: MS4525, `pitot_scale = 1.0`, a differential pressure of 245 Pa. Then the scale was set to 1.1. What speeds does INAV show?
options: 20.0 m/s, then 22.0 m/s: the scale multiplies the speed
20.0 m/s, then 21.0 m/s: the scale multiplies the pressure under the root
14.1 m/s, then 15.6 m/s: ΔP / 1.225 under the root without the factor of two
20.0 m/s, then 24.2 m/s: the scale enters squared
questions.explain: V = `pitot_scale` × √(2 × |ΔP| / 1.225). √(490 / 1.225) = 20 m/s; the scale is in front of the root, so 1.1 gives 22 m/s. Hence the correction rule: new scale = old × reference speed / indicated speed.

questions.q: `pitot_hardware = VIRTUAL`. Ground speed 18 m/s, nose at 90°, the wind vector of the estimator: 5 m/s, direction 270°. What is the airspeed?
options: 13 m/s: the wind is subtracted from the ground speed
18 m/s: without a sensor the ground speed is taken
18.7 m/s: the square root of the sum of the squares of 18 and 5
23 m/s: it is a headwind, and the speeds add up
questions.explain: The wind vector shows where the air is moving to. The tailwind component is W × cos(270° − 90°) = −5 m/s, and the airspeed = 18 − (−5) = 23 m/s. That is how `virtualPitotCalculate()` computes it.

questions.q: The OSD element of an external LM75 sensor (slot 0, address 0) has to blink above 85 °C. Which line is correct?
options: `temp_sensor 0 1 0 -20 85 2 ESC`
`temp_sensor 0 2 0 -200 850 2 ESC`
`temp_sensor 0 1 0 -200 850 2 ESC`
`temp_sensor 0 1 0x48 -200 8500 2 ESC`
questions.explain: Type 1 is LM75, the address is a number 0–7, the thresholds are in tenths of a degree: 85 °C = 850, and −550 to 1250 is allowed. Type 2 is a DS18B20 with a 16-digit ROM. The number 85 would mean 8.5 °C, and 8500 is out of range and gives a parse error.

questions.q: A fixed wing, `apa_pow = 120`, `fw_reference_airspeed = 1500`. The pitot tube is partly blocked and shows 10 m/s at a real 20 m/s. What happens to the P, D and FF gains?
options: They grow by a factor of 1.63 instead of dropping to 0.71: a risk of oscillation
They do not change: APA works only on the virtual airspeed
They drop to 0.3: the lower limit of the factor applies
They drop to 0.71, as they should at 20 m/s: there is no error in the gains
questions.explain: Factor = (1500 / V)^1.2. From the reading of 1000 cm/s it is 1.5^1.2 = 1.63, while at the real 2000 cm/s it should be 0.75^1.2 = 0.71. The gains are 2.3 times higher than needed. The GPS check of the pitot triggers only below 30 % of the virtual airspeed, and here it is 50 %.
